sentences.text: Potamornis was a heavily built bird weighing approximately 1.5 to 2 kilograms, similar to other diving species.
Fossils of this animal were found in the Lance Formation at Buck Creek in the USA.
Possible remains were also found in the upper Hell Creek Formation of Montana, though these may have been reworked from the Danian age of the Paleogene period.
The only known species, Potamornis skutchi, was named and described in 2001 by Elzanowski, Paul & Stidham.
Potamornis is classified within the subclass Hesperornithes.
It is almost certainly a member of the Hesperornithes, a group of hefty, toothed, flightless diving birds from the Mesozoic seas.
Cladistic analysis suggests Potamornis shares more unique traits with the family Hesperornithidae than other aspects of its anatomy might imply.
Potamornis lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
Researchers suggest that flightlessness within the Hesperornithes may have evolved independently in different lineages, including Potamornis.
